sentences.text: Long ago, people were paid... just to wake other people up.
And this was a real job!
In Britain, during the Industrial Revolution, factory workers had to wake up before dawn.
The problem? Alarm clocks were expensive and rare.
So a strange profession was born, the "knocker-upper."
Every morning before sunrise, they walked the streets with a long stick, tapping on their customers' bedroom windows.
Tap... tap... tap...
"Okay, okay! I'm awake!"
And don't even try pretending.
They wouldn't leave until they were sure you were really up.
Some were even more creative.
One woman in London was famous for using a pea shooter... firing dried peas at windows.
Tik! Tik! Tik!
The pay? Just a few pennies a week.
But wait... if their job was waking people up, who woke up the knocker-upper?
The answer? Many of them worked through the night.
They stayed awake, and only went to bed after all their customers were up.
The job slowly disappeared once alarm clocks became cheap.
And today? We have alarms on our phones... and still hit snooze five times.
Are you an instant riser, or Team Snooze? Tell me in the comments!
